notes.claim: Power factor is the cosine of the angle between real power and apparent power, kW over kVA.
True power and apparent power form the adjacent and hypotenuse of a right triangle, so the power factor is the cosine of the phase angle.
In one worked 230 V example, power factor 0.6 gives a line current of 72.5 A and correcting to 0.8 reduces it to 54.5 A (source's "20 per cent" is loose: about 25 per cent).

sources.title: Power Factor
sources.quote: Power Factor is the cosine of the angle between the Real Power and the Apparent Power; kW/kVa pf = kW/kVa = cos(φ)

sources.title: Calculating Power Factor | Power Factor | Electronics Textbook
sources.quote: Because true power and apparent power form the adjacent and hypotenuse sides of a right triangle, respectively, the power factor ratio is also equal to the cosine of that phase angle.

sources.title: Power Triangle and Power Factor in AC Circuits | Electrical A2Z
sources.quote: If the power factor of the load is 0.6 (cos 53°), the total current in the line will be 72.5 A. Correcting the PF to 0.8 (cos 37°) would reduce the current to 54.5 A
